question: How much independently measured scanner-matrix error can the P4CR physical inverse tolerate before recovered dye-layer correlation is no longer reliable?

simulation.order: correlated developed density -> transmittance -> true scanner matrix -> inverse of independently perturbed scanner matrix -> recovered density correlation

selection.development_rule: largest frozen error level whose worst seed-direction correlation RMSE is at most 0.01

execution_amendment: Before any simulated row was scored, matrix-only feasibility showed that the originally listed 0.08 and 0.16 perturbations made one scanner matrix contain negative coefficients, contradicting the frozen positive-matrix domain. Those two levels were removed; all directions, remaining levels, seeds, thresholds and selection rules are unchanged.
forbidden: change levels, directions, seeds or thresholds after development or confirmation
fit scanner perturbations to simulated layer truth
interpret the selected synthetic tolerance as a measured scanner calibration uncertainty
map this result to a stock, scanner profile, renderer default or product state
claim_ceiling: Controlled float64 sensitivity evidence for P4CR layer-correlation recovery under frozen scanner-matrix perturbations; not real scanner calibration, dye-layer measurement, stock truth or product evidence.
